headline: Discussed 505 Riverside Avenue site planning, a wetlands buffer amendment, and a revised specimen tree map; approved only past meeting minutes.
summary: Members discussed planning for the 505 Riverside Avenue site after demolition, with property conveyance to the city likely in early 2027. They also discussed a wetlands amendment, a possible letter to the Planning Commission this winter, and a revised specimen tree map. The only vote was to approve the September 14 and October 5, 2026 minutes, 6-0-0.
decisions: Approved the September 14 and October 5, 2026 minutes 6-0.

Conservation Board Meeting Minutes 
Monday, November 2, 2026 – 5:30 pm 
Remote & In-Person Meeting 
 
Attendance   
 Board Members: Rebecca Roman (RR), Zoe Richards (ZR), Alan Reichard (AR), Kelly Farrell (KF), 
Evan Horne (EH), Lee Toomey (LT) 
 Absent: Ryan Crehan (RC), Dale Azaria (DA) 
 Public: Sharon Bushor 
 Staff: Scott Gustin (Permitting & Inspections), Dan Cahill  (Parks & Rec) 
 
RR, chair, called the meeting to order at 5:32 p.m.  
 
Minutes 
 
September 14 and October 5, 2026 minutes 
 
A MOTION was made by AR and SECONDED by KF: 
 
Approve the minutes as written. 
 
Vote: 6-0-0, motion carried.     
 
Board Comment 
 
RR noted this Thursday’s PlanBTV2050 open house at the High School.  She encouraged members to 
attend.   
 
ZR asked if the Urban Reserve will be up for discussion at the open house.  SG replied that it will be.  
Dan Cahill said that the Urban Reserve is a focus area of the comp plan.  He noted the requirement to log 
an official map of the Urban Reserve per the conservation easement.  Once that’s done, then t he city can 
move ahead with determining future uses of the Urban Reserve.   
 
RR requested 3 BCB members for the NBCS grant application review.  RR is one.  KF & EH volunteered.   
 
EH requested the full BCB see all of the applications before the meeting.  Dan Cahill said we can 
probably do that to make sure everyone has the same information.   
 
EH plugged the environmental issue training, Unit 2 provided by VT ANR.  He thanked ZR and Dan for 
attending the Ward 1 NPA.  He felt from the Ward 1 NPA meeting that there is interest in more 
information and more participation in spreading the word and doing the implementation work.   
 
Public Comment 
 
Sharon Bushor spoke about housing and open space.  These two things go together.  They are not in 
opposition.  There needs to be an understanding that full funding of the Conservation Legacy Fund is not 
a frivolous ask.  Our open spaces become more and more important with increasing development

November 2, 2026 - pg. 2 
   
pressure.  Regarding the urban reserve, she does not know what the future hold s.  When the interim 
management plan was put in place, 20 years was anticipated before revisiting.  Its been much more than 
that.  We need to find an advocate on the City Council.   
 
Update & Discussion 
 
1. 505 Riverside Avenue Hazard Mitigation Grant 
Planning for post-demolition and site re-naturalization 
 
RR noted the unstable conditions of the Riverside Avenue slope.  ZR provided some additional 
background and history and mentioned the extensive use of trash and organic fill in decades past.   
 
SG gave an overview of the site and the process.  Several years ago, the property owners approached 
the city about a buy-out of the property due to the deteriorating conditions of the building and the slope 
beneath it.  A geotechnical analysis of the site was done a couple of years ago and it was determined that 
the property was in imminent risk of slide.  As such, the property was eligible for consideration under 
FEMA’s hazard mitigation grant program (HMGP).  An application was filed with VT DEM, and FEMA 
ultimately approved the application.  At this point, an appraisal has been done and the parties are moving 
towards conveyance of the property to the city, likely sometime in early 2027.  Demolition will take place 
in the 2027 construction season and will remove the building and all of the asphalt.  Contract 
requirements will result in a stabilized site; however, there is opportunity here to introduce some native 
plantings to the property.   
 
Dan Cahill said RC can help with procurement of native plants for the propert y.   
 
RR, would it be possible for some BCB members to partake in a planting day?   
 
KF, can a sitting bench be installed?   
 
LT, can the planting plan include something to reflect the agriculture / agroforestry activities in the 
interval? 
 
Dan said he likes the idea of involving others in the community in plating the site.  
 
2. Miscellaneous Updates 
Revised Specimen Tree map 
 
SG noted one of the action items in the new Open Space Plan is to identify locations of specimen trees in 
the city.  An initial map was done a few months ago and, based on SAL’s urban canopy data, selected for 
the top 10% of trees in the city per tree height and canopy diameter.  It was suggested that the basis for 
the map be revised to be more focused on tree canopy diameter, as there are a number of tall skinny 
trees (such as white pines) that may skew the map.  This revised specimen tree map is based primarily 
on canopy diameter with limited exclusion based on height. The map is intended as a reference for permit 
application review and, therefore, does not include the RCO (conservation) zones.  
 
LT, is there a way for anyone to add trees to the map?  Like the state’s big tree program.  KF, maybe 
have a DBH threshold for consideration of inclusion in the map.  SG said we could use the bas e metric for 
specimen trees as defined in the ordinance for inclusion in the specimen tree map.   
 
KF, if we confirm if things are specimen trees or not, maybe codify that in the map. 
 
Vegetation Ordinance status 
 
SG said that the pending amendments to the Vegetation Ordinance will be up for just a procedural 
discussion at this coming Friday’s City Council Ordinance Committee meeting.  He will keep the Board 
posted as it moves ahead for discussion by the Ordinance Committee at a future date.
Conservation Board Minutes 
November 2, 2026 - pg. 3 
   
 
Wetlands amendment 
 
SG overviewed the process and background of the wetlands amendment.  The BCB approved an 
updated city wetlands map in April to incorporate the new state wetlands map .  It was taken up for initial 
consideration by the Planning Commission in September and scheduled for open discussion and possible 
referral to public hearing in early October.  Let’s Build Homes submitted a letter to the Planning 
Commission for consideration at their October 6 meeting.  The letter isn’t so much aimed at the map 
revision as it is aimed at reducing the current 100’ wetland buffer to 25’ consistent with state standards in 
identified growth areas.  The letter also seems to address the 100’ buffer as a proposal (but it is not new).   
 
SG noted that additional lands subject to wetlands review are minimal (new state wetland polygons that 
do not overlap with existing city polygons).  He is looking to quantify these additional lands.  Any state 
polygon that overlaps with a city polygon is of no new regulatory consequence, as they depict the same 
wetland that would be subject to an onsite delineation to determine exact boundaries in the event of a 
development proposal.    
 
KF, we’re not adding wetlands.  We’re just making it consistent with the sate map.  There’s lots of data 
indicating that more than a 25’ buffer is needed for protection.  If this letter made the process pause, that 
means folks do not fully understand.   
 
EH, feels like there needs to be something from the BCB in response to the Let’s Build Homes letter.  
What does a 25’ vs 100’ buffer look like?   
 
SG noted that the buffer is not a setback.  The BCB has reviewed and approved applications within a 
buffer.  Typically conditions are improved.   
 
ZR has heard that all of the administrative burden previously at Act 250 will land on the city if Tier 1A 
status is attained. 
 
SG said we should aim to circle back with the Planning Commission this winter with a letter, quantitative 
data, and a couple of Board members to attend. EH will put together an initial draft.  SG will aim to have 
the GIS analysis done before Thanksgiving. 
 
Urban Reserve in the Comprehensive Plan 
 
This item was covered in Board Comment above.   
 
March 2027 follow-up Stakeholder Summit 
 
SG said that the new Open Space Plan was adopted earlier this year.  Putting that plan together included 
a number of stakeholder discussions.  He and Dan talked about hosting a follow up summit with those 
stakeholders in March to talk about what implementation has been done so far, what’s in progress, and 
what things should be prioritized for tackling next.  KF asked if this would be open to BCB members.  SG 
replied that it would be.   
 
Adjournment 
6:52 PM.
